theater: 翁布利亞佩魯西亞山城

battle.name: 佩魯辛戰爭
battle.theater: 翁布利亞佩魯西亞山城
battle.brief: 公元前41年，安東尼派的意大利軍隊退守佩魯西亞，遭奧克塔維安大軍圍城，於前40年3月陷落。守軍曾借安息騎兵與安東尼派援軍牽制三頭同盟，圍城以饑荒與夜襲火攻收場，城破後數百元老與騎士在凱撒祭壇前被殺。卡面的埃及月牙劍屬青銅時代單刃彎刀，前41年早已退出戰場；羅馬軍團實際用的是短劍、標槍與大盾。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 這是公元前41至前40年羅馬共和國的一次內戰，交戰的兩端都在三頭同盟內部：以東方行省為資源的安東尼派，對上掌握意大利與西屬行省的奧克塔維安；實際戰場在翁布利亞的山城佩魯西亞及其周邊。安東尼在意大利的總督盧基烏斯·安東尼與其妻福莉維婭率領從意大利徵召的八個軍團，與翁布利亞人的武裝結合；城內還有安東尼部將弗爾維烏斯·弗拉庫斯所部，以及被圍的市民武裝。第三方是安息（帕提）王國：佩魯西亞人向安息求援，叛羅馬的將軍昆圖斯·拉比厄斯在安息王庭取得支持，率帕提騎兵越過阿爾卑斯山進入意大利，把三頭同盟的注意力拉成南北兩線。此外還有安東尼派以外的一層：佩魯西亞人曾派使向馬爾庫斯·布魯圖斯與卡西烏斯求助，把城市交給流亡的「解放者」，公開挑戰三頭同盟的合法性。編制上，安東尼與奧克塔維安各以超級執政官權力（imperium proconsulare）領兵，佩魯西亞一方則是城邦民兵加安東尼派駐軍的混合編制，沒有常設的統一指揮系統。
countriesEn: This was a civil war inside the Roman Republic between 41 and 40 BC, and the clash took place within the Second Triumvirate itself: the Antonian side, drawing on the resources of the eastern provinces, against Octavian, who held Italy and the western provinces. The fighting theatre was the hill town of Perusia in Umbria and the country around it. Lucius Antonius, the brother of Mark Antony and governor of Italy, together with his wife Fulvia, led eight legions levied in Italy, and these were combined with the armed men of Perusia; inside the walls were also the detachment of the Antonian legate Fulvius Flaccus and the besieged citizens' militia. The third party was the Parthian (Arsacid) kingdom: Perusia appealed to Parthia, and the renegade Roman general Quintus Labienus obtained the support of the Parthian court, leading Parthian cavalry over the Alps into Italy and splitting the attention of the triumvirs into two separate theatres. A further layer ran outside both camps: the Perusians sent envoys to Marcus Brutus and Cassius, offering the city to the exiled Liberators and openly challenging the legitimacy of the triumvirate. In terms of structure, Antony and Octavian each commanded armies under the super-proconsular power (imperium proconsulare), while on the Perusian side there was no unified command structure at all, only a mixture of a civic militia and the Antonian garrison.
people: 三方各有決策者。安東尼一方：馬克·安東尼本人在東方行省遙控，以命令徵召兵員、徵發款項，並把佩魯西亞交給部將弗爾維烏斯·弗拉庫斯；其弟盧基烏斯·安東尼在公元前41年出任執政官，是意大利的實際主持人，他與福莉維婭率八個軍團入意大利，佔領羅馬後退守佩魯西亞；福莉維婭是整場衝突的推手之一，她主張安東尼獨佔羅馬，多次在軍中與政治場合推動對奧克塔維安的鬥爭，圍城結束後被逐出意大利，流亡希臘的西基翁，公元前40年死於該地。另有馬庫斯·安東尼（人稱「雄辯家」）在伊特魯里亞活動，是佩魯西亞一方的羅馬人望。奧克塔維安一方由他本人直接指揮圍城，昆圖斯·沙爾維迪埃努斯·魯弗斯奉命掃蕩拉丁平原而未能與主力會合，奧盧斯·普勞提烏斯在北意大利擊潰拉比厄斯，擋住了安息方向的援軍。佩魯西亞方面有弗拉庫斯、盧基烏斯·卡尼尼烏斯·加盧斯等一批安東尼派軍官，以及主持民政的當地議會。留下記錄的還有西塞罗，他以書信譏諷福莉維婭的所為；事後蘇托尼烏斯與卡西烏斯·狄奧記下了城破後的屠殺，以及「佩魯西亞祭壇」的由來。
peopleEn: Each side had its own decision-makers. On the Antonian side: Mark Antony himself, in control from the eastern provinces, who gave the orders to levy troops and money and left Perusia in the hands of his legate Fulvius Flaccus; his brother Lucius Antonius, consul in 41 BC, was the effective manager of Italy, and it was he who entered Italy with eight legions together with Fulvia, occupied Rome and then withdrew to Perusia; Fulvia was one of the driving forces of the whole affair, arguing that Antony should rule Rome alone and pushing the confrontation with Octavian both in the camp and in politics, and after the siege she was driven out of Italy and exiled to Sicyon in Greece, where she died in 40 BC. Marcus Antonius, called the Orator, was active in Etruria and was a Roman notable of the Perusian side. Octavian's side was commanded by himself in person during the siege; Quintus Salvius Salvidienus Rufus was ordered to sweep the Latin plain but failed to join the main force, while Aulus Plautius defeated Labienus in northern Italy and blocked the reinforcements coming from the Parthian direction. On the Perusian side stood a number of Antonian officers such as Flaccus and Lucius Caninius Gallus, together with the local council that administered the city's affairs. Among those who left a record is Cicero, who mocked Fulvia's doings in his letters; and afterwards Suetonius and Cassius Dio recorded the slaughter that followed the fall of the city, and the origin of the Arae Perusinae.
kits: 卡面兵器是埃及月牙劍（khopesh）：青銅時代的單刃彎刀，弧度外張、刃口內凹，砍入後不需拔刀，約公元前1500年已在埃及軍隊服役，至新王國後期才被直刃雙鋒劍取代。公元前41年的佩魯西亞沒有任何一支部隊配備月牙劍——它已是古物，只能作為「單刃彎刀」這一系的源頭來看；同一血統在戰場上的後裔是伊比利亞的 falcata 與色雷斯的 machaira，兩者都隨羅馬的輔助部隊作戰。真正上陣的是羅馬制式裝備：步兵用短劍（gladius）與長七首（pugio），投槍兵配標槍（pila），大盾（scutum）掩護正面；甲冑有環節甲（lorica segmentata）、鎖子甲（lorica hamata）與鱗甲（lorica squamata），頭盔有蒙提福爾蒂諾式、帝國高盧式與弗里吉亞式，足著 caligae，軍旗為 signa 與金翅鷹（aquila）。攻城方面靠工程兵與隨軍工匠架設的 vineae、箭塔，以及配重投石機（onager）與車弩（carroballista），其規格可從維特魯威《建築十書》第十卷的記述推知。安息方面是複合弓、康托斯長槍、札甲與鎧馬具，騎兵用彎刀與長矛。佩魯西亞守軍則混合安東尼派軍團裝備與市民自備的長矛、砍刀，投石索手不多、攻城器械極少，糧食靠城內存糧與周邊鄉村供給。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Egyptian khopesh: a single-edged bronze sword whose blade curves outward and whose edge is concave, so that it does not have to be pulled back out after a blow, in Egyptian service from about 1500 BC and displaced by straight double-edged blades late in the New Kingdom. No unit at Perusia in 41 BC carried a khopesh — by then it was an antiquity, and it can only be read as the ancestor of the single-edged curved sword family; the surviving descendants of the same line on the battlefield were the Iberian falcata and the Thracian machaira, both carried by Roman auxiliaries. What actually went into battle was the Roman standard equipment: short swords (gladius) and long daggers (pugio) for the infantry, javelins (pila) for the skirmishers, the large curved scutum to cover the front, armour in the form of segmentata plates, mail (lorica hamata) and scale (lorica squamata), helmets of Montefortino, Imperial Gallic and Phrygian types, caligae on the feet, and signa with the aquila as the standards. For the siege the engineers and attached craftsmen raised vineae and siege towers and worked the onager and the carroballista, whose characteristics can be reconstructed from the description in the tenth book of Vitruvius' De architectura. The Parthians used composite bows, the kontos, scale armour and horse trappings, their cavalry fighting with curved swords and long spears. The Perusian defenders mixed Antonian legionary kit with spears and chopping blades bought or made by the townsmen; they had few slingers, almost no siege equipment, and drew their food from stores inside the walls and from the surrounding countryside.
tactics: 戰術層面是一場典型的羅馬內戰攻城，但夾雜三方博弈。安東尼派先用政治手段接管意大利：盧基烏斯·安東尼以八個軍團佔領羅馬，靠拖延與談判把戰爭拉長；士兵欠餉、要求退役，屢次在城中的公共場所集結，安東尼派無法單靠命令壓住。佩魯西亞方則採守城加外援的雙線：城內以石造城牆與山丘地形固守，等安息騎兵北上製造第二戰場；安息軍以帕提式的戰略——游騎掠地、切斷交通、逼迫敵軍分兵——進入意大利，令奧克塔維安不得不分兵，拉比厄斯一度威脅到羅馬的安全。奧克塔維安的對策是集中：他不追擊游騎，而以主力穩住佩魯西亞，派普勞提烏斯處理北方，然後圍城。圍城的基本手段是封鎖——控制通往山城的道路、切斷糧道，冬季到來後城內出現饑荒；同時以工程兵推進攻城器械與箭塔射擊。最後是夜襲：進攻方在外圍堆積的柴草與帳幕上放火，火勢照亮城牆，守軍在黑暗中崩潰，城門被突破。城破之後的處置則不留情面：蘇托尼烏斯記載奧克塔維安饒過普通士兵與多數市民，但仍有一批被標記的元老與騎士在凱撒祭壇前被殺。
tacticsEn: In tactical terms this was a classic Roman civil-war siege, complicated by a three-cornered contest. The Antonians first took Italy by political means: Lucius Antonius occupied Rome with eight legions and relied on delay and negotiation to prolong the war; the soldiers were unpaid, demanded their discharge, and repeatedly assembled in the public places of the city, and the Antonian leadership could not hold them down by orders alone. The Perusians adopted a two-pronged scheme of holding the city and seeking foreign help: inside the walls they relied on stone curtain walls and hill terrain, while waiting for Parthian cavalry to move north and create a second theatre. The Parthian force entered Italy with the Parthian method — riding wide, cutting communications, forcing the enemy to divide — which obliged Octavian to detach troops, and Labienus for a time threatened Rome itself. Octavian's answer was concentration: he did not chase the raiders, but fixed Perusia with his main body, left Plautius to deal with the north, and then sat down before the city. The basic method of the siege was blockade — controlling the roads that led to the hill town, cutting the supply lines, so that famine appeared inside the walls once winter set in — while the engineers pushed forward artillery and siege towers. The end came with a night assault: the attackers fired the brushwood and tents stacked outside the defences, the firelight lit the walls, the defenders collapsed in the darkness and the gate was forced. The treatment of the defeated was not merciful: Suetonius records that Octavian pardoned the ordinary soldiers and most of the citizens, but a number of senators and knights who had been marked down were killed before the altar of Caesar.
data: 可核對的數字有限，只能列出有史料依據者。安東尼一方在意大利徵召的部隊，史料記為八個軍團，這是佩魯西亞防軍的主幹。圍城自公元前41年冬延續到前40年3月，最後以饑荒迫使守方投降；城市陷落與大量處決集中在3月，蘇托尼烏斯與卡西烏斯·狄奧都把處決的時點記在3月15日，被送上「佩魯西亞祭壇」（Arae Perusinae）的元老與騎士人數記為三百。地理上，佩魯西亞在翁布利亞境內，舊城立於海拔約五百米的山丘群上，距羅馬沿弗拉米尼亞大道約一百六十餘公里，控扼台伯河上游與通往北意大利的通道。安息干涉的規模不大，拉比厄斯所部是以帕提騎兵為主、雜以高盧人的混合縱隊，遠不足以單獨攻戰意大利，但足以把三頭同盟的軍隊拉成兩線。佩魯西亞守軍的實際人數、被圍市民的數目與攻城時的傷亡數，古代各家均未留下可靠記載；起事的確切月份也沒有被保存下來，一般只以公元前41年計。月牙劍的形制則可確知：青銅、單刃、外彎，通行年代約在公元前1600年至前1000年之間，出土例集中於埃及，與佩魯西亞戰場沒有直接關係。
dataEn: The verifiable figures are limited, and only those with a documentary basis can be listed. The Antonian troops levied in Italy are recorded as eight legions, and these formed the backbone of the Perusian defence. The siege ran from the winter of 41 BC into March 40 BC and ended when famine forced the defenders to surrender; the fall of the city and the mass executions are concentrated in March, and both Suetonius and Cassius Dio place the executions on 15 March, with three hundred senators and knights being led to the Arae Perusinae, the altars of Perusia. Geographically, Perusia lay in Umbria, the old town standing on a group of hills about five hundred metres above sea level, some hundred and sixty kilometres or so from Rome along the Via Flaminia, controlling the upper Tiber valley and the road to northern Italy. The scale of the Parthian intervention was small: Labienus commanded a mixed column of Parthian horsemen and Gauls, far too weak to conquer Italy on its own, but enough to pull the triumviral armies into two separate fronts. No reliable figure survives from the ancient writers for the actual size of the Perusian garrison, for the number of besieged citizens, or for the casualties of the siege; the exact month of the rising was not preserved either and is generally given simply as 41 BC. The form of the khopesh, by contrast, is well established: bronze, single-edged, curving outward, in use roughly between 1600 and 1000 BC, with its excavated examples concentrated in Egypt and no direct connection to the battlefield of Perusia.
cause: 直接起因是伊特魯里亞的社會與政治怨恨。佩魯西亞在共和國時期是羅馬殖民地，城外大片土地在布魯圖斯與卡西烏斯戰敗後被沒收，用來安置奧克塔維安的退伍軍人；被沒收的田莊、稅負與安置名額都落在翁布利亞的城鎮上，怨恨由來已久。奧克塔維安在公元前42年出任執政官時派斯克里博尼烏斯·利博出任伊特魯里亞總督，以佩魯西亞為駐地，他的駐軍與徵收方式又加深了對立。公元前41年安東尼下令部將弗拉庫斯到佩魯西亞徵集兵員與款項，佩魯西亞人拒絕，衝突中弗拉庫斯退入城內反被圍困——這是起事直接的導火線。背後更有三頭同盟體制的張力：安東尼與奧克塔維安在東方與西方的資源分配上早有裂痕，意大利交由盧基烏斯·安東尼節制，更讓安東尼派以為可趁勢獨占意大利；福莉維婭在軍中與政治場合的操作，以及士卒欠餒、要求退役的風潮，則把衝突推向前線。佩魯西亞人把希望寄托在兩處：向安息求援以牽制三頭同盟，向馬爾庫斯·布魯圖斯與卡西烏斯示好以博取政治名分，於是這場起事同時帶有反三頭同盟與反安東尼派的雙重色彩。
causeEn: The immediate cause lay in the social and political grievances of Etruria. In the Republican period Perusia was a Roman colony, and large tracts of land around the city were confiscated after the defeat of Brutus and Cassius in order to settle Octavian's veterans; the confiscated estates, the taxes and the allotments of settlement land all fell on the towns of Umbria, and the resentment was of long standing. When Octavian was consul in 42 BC he sent Scribonius Libo to govern Etruria with his seat at Perusia, and the garrison and the way Libo levied contributions deepened the hostility. In 41 BC Antony ordered his legate Flaccus to Perusia to muster troops and money; the Perusians refused, and in the ensuing fighting Flaccus was driven back inside the city and himself surrounded — the immediate spark of the rising. Behind it lay the strain inside the triumviral settlement: the division of resources between Antony and Octavian in the east and the west had been open since the start, and the assignment of Italy to Lucius Antonius encouraged the Antonians to think they could seize Italy for themselves; Fulvia's manoeuvring in the camp and in politics, together with the arrears of the soldiers and the agitation for discharge, pushed the conflict to the front line. The Perusians placed their hopes in two directions: an appeal to Parthia to pin the triumvirs down, and an approach to Marcus Brutus and Cassius in order to gain political credit, so that the rising carried both an anti-triunviral and an anti-Antonian colouring at once.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果遠超出翁布利亞的山城本身。第一，行省城市第一次顯示可以用外力（傭兵、金屬、帕提騎兵）撬動意大利的內政，並且得到安東尼派內部的部分支持；羅馬此後對行省徵兵與安置退伍軍人的做法備受爭議。第二，「佩魯西亞祭壇」成為三頭同盟清洗的樣板：奧克塔維安在城破後區分對待普通士兵與市民、以及被標記的元老與騎士，前者開釋、後者殺害，此一先例在隨後的清洗與公元前30年代前的政治鬥爭中不斷被援引。第三，安東尼派因此在意大利立足失敗：盧基烏斯·安東尼被外派西班牙行省，福莉維婭被逐出意大利並死於西基翁；安東尼失去了在意大利的直屬軍隊與政治網絡。第四，這也是安東尼與奧克塔維安同盟破裂前的最後修補：兩人和解，並以安東尼迎娶屋大維的妹妹屋大維婭作象徵，於公元前37年延長三頭同盟的期限；但這段和平在公元前36年安東尼的帕提戰役與前32年的阿克提姆戰役之後全面崩潰，佩魯西亞的慘劇因而成為內戰循環中的一個節點，而不是終點。最後，它在編年史中的位置，是三頭同盟時期意大利政治第一次被拉到明面，也是「解放者」事業在意大利本土留下的最後一場有組織的軍事回響。
impactEn: The consequences of this war reached far beyond the hill town in Umbria. First, an Italian provincial city showed for the first time that foreign force — mercenaries, money, Parthian cavalry — could pry open the politics of Italy, and that it could do so with at least partial support from inside the Antonian camp; the Roman practice of recruiting in the provinces and settling veterans there became a standing grievance. Second, the Arae Perusinae became a model for triumviral purge: after the city fell, Octavian treated the ordinary soldiers and most of the citizens differently from the senators and knights who had been marked down, pardoning the former and killing the latter, and that precedent was invoked repeatedly in the purges and in the political struggles of the years before 30 BC. Third, the Antonians lost their footing in Italy: Lucius Antonius was sent out to a Spanish province, Fulvia was driven out of Italy and died at Sicyon, and Antony lost both his own troops and his political network in the peninsula. Fourth, this was the last repair of the alliance between Antony and Octavian before it finally broke: the two were reconciled, the union was symbolised by Antony's marriage to Octavian's sister Octavia, and the term of the triumvirate was extended to 37 BC; but this peace collapsed completely after Antony's Parthian campaign of 36 BC and the Battle of Actium in 32 BC, so that the catastrophe of Perusia was a link in the cycle of civil war rather than its end. Finally, its place in the chronicle is that the politics of Italy was brought openly into the foreground for the first time in the period of the triumvirate, and that this was the last organised military echo of the Liberators' cause on Italian soil.
result: 公元前40年3月，奧克塔維安的大軍完成對佩魯西亞的最後攻擊，城市投降。圍城以饑荒削弱守軍、以夜襲與火攻打開缺口，最後一批守軍在城牆與城內被殲滅或被殺，未投降者部分當場死亡、部分逃亡。城破之後，奧克塔維安赦免了大部分普通士兵與市民，但把一批元老與騎士押到為凱撒所設的祭壇前屠殺，蘇托尼烏斯與狄奧都記下了這一段，並留下「佩魯西亞祭壇」之名。安東尼一方的高層隨即被拆散：盧基烏斯·安東尼調往西班牙行省，名上是讓他鎮守一側、實為調離；福莉維婭被送往西基翁，翌年病逝；佩魯西亞人接應布魯圖斯與卡西烏斯的政治指望，也隨城陷落而落空。戰爭以安東尼派在意大利的慘敗告終：佩魯西亞不再是可據以號召意大利的據點，奧克塔維安則藉此鞏固了他在意大利與西部的基地，並迫使安東尼接受更緊密的同盟安排——這套安排維持到公元前37年，然後在安東尼對帕提的勝利與隨後的分裂中崩解。從編年史的角度看，佩魯辛戰爭是羅馬共和國內戰從「元老院與執政官」轉入「三頭同盟直接以軍隊和行省決鬥」的關節點，也是屋大維日後道路上第一次靠圍城取勝的重大勝利。
resultEn: In March 40 BC the army of Octavian delivered the final assault on Perusia and the city surrendered. The siege had weakened the defenders with famine and opened a breach with a night attack and fire, and the last of the defenders were killed at the walls and inside the city, the unsurrendered dying on the spot or escaping. After the fall, Octavian pardoned most of the ordinary soldiers and citizens, but a number of senators and knights were driven to the altar set up for Caesar and slaughtered, and both Suetonius and Dio recorded this, leaving behind the name of the Arae Perusinae. The leadership of the Antonian side was then broken up: Lucius Antonius was transferred to a Spanish province, nominally to hold one flank and in fact to remove him from Italy; Fulvia was sent to Sicyon and died there of illness the following year; and the Perusian hope of bringing in Brutus and Cassius collapsed with the city. The war ended in a severe defeat for the Antonians in Italy: Perusia was no longer a point from which Italy could be called, while Octavian consolidated his base in Italy and the west and forced Antony to accept a much tighter alliance — an arrangement that held until 37 BC and then broke apart after Antony's victory over Parthia and the division that followed. From the point of view of the chronicle, the Perusine War is the hinge at which Roman civil war passed from the senate and the consuls to the triumvirs deciding matters directly with armies and provinces, and it is also the first great siege victory on the road that would make Octavian Augustus.
